title: The Nordic Model Under Deglobalization

The Nordic Model Under Deglobalization

August Gudmundsson

Gavekal Research | 22 Sep 2026

As Sweden moves on from its recent election, its economy is also emerging from the struggles that began in 2022. Domestic demand is recovering and manufacturing has proved surprisingly resilient. But with the global economy becoming less integrated and fears of a new Europe-centered “China shock” mounting, the question is whether Sweden and its Nordic peers can sustain that recovery.The shared weakness looks troubling given that all three economies are built on a similar model. The Nordics, excluding oil-rich Norway, derived their prosperity from selling a diversified range of products to the world, with persistent current account surpluses going hand in hand with fiscal restraint at home, much like their cousin Germany. Geopolitical fragmentation, trade wars and Chinese competition should therefore leave them unusually exposed. And indeed, with four-year growth averaging just 1% in Sweden, stagnating in Finland and flattered by a single pharmaceutical company’s boom in Denmark, the Nordics might seem another expression of Germany’s industrial malaise.
